key_insight: A physics-grounded welding digital twin combines thermal simulation, AI surrogates, and robot control to screen in-space joining strategies before experimental testing.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could support adaptive welding control as robot travel speed changes, helping maintain weld geometry during on-orbit assembly and repair.
method: Finite-volume thermal model includes phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates predict weld responses; gravity is assessed separately via a hydrostatic-to-capillary pressure ratio.
Simulated six-axis robot uses proportional power-setting control along an L-shaped seam.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs in repeated five-fold cross-validation; finite-volume re-evaluation placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative 1–3 mm root-side-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop validation remain necessary.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
